title: Simple Present vs. Present Continuous
explanation: Use the simple present for habits and general facts (I work every day). Use the present continuous (am/is/are + -ing) for actions happening right now (I am working right now).

title: Articles: a, an, the
explanation: Use 'a' before consonant sounds and 'an' before vowel sounds for something non-specific. Use 'the' when both speakers know exactly which one you mean.

examples.text: I saw the dog we talked about.

title: Question Formation with Do/Does
explanation: For simple present questions with most verbs, use 'do' (I/you/we/they) or 'does' (he/she/it) plus the base verb.

title: Common Irregular Verbs
explanation: Many common verbs don't follow the regular -ed past tense pattern and must be memorized.
